subject: Infra allocations roadmap, SLAs, and price-elasticity notes
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-data.com, sarah@bigcloud.co
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Infra allocations roadmap, SLAs, and price-elasticity notes

Team — kicking off a short thread to align on the QBR deliverable related to infra capacity and unit economics. Attaching the working allocations matrix and a draft of the QBR slides for reference. High-level asks: 

- Confirm committed capacity tiers (reserved vs burst) for next quarter and proposed SLA targets per tier.
- Provide a short table (by Monday) of expected GPU spend and utilization per model-family for baseline and surge scenarios. Include assumptions on sequence length and RT percentiles.
- Run a 1-week sensitivity on batching and KV-cache hit improvements (suggest +10/20/30% hit) and show $/1k tokens delta.
- Propose a fallback plan: explicit model variant mapping for low/high capacity windows so product can degrade gracefully.

Please put owners on each bullet — I want this consolidated into a single slide we can present to the execs on Friday.

Attachments: allocations_matrix_v3.xlsx (tabbed: baseline / surge / price-elasticity), qbr_slide_draft_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Infra allocations roadmap, SLAs, and price-elasticity notes

Lauren — quick responses inline and owners proposed: 

- Committed capacity tiers: we can freeze the baseline reserved pool at current commit for Q3 (owner: jonas). For burst, propose a soft cap tied to spot availability and cross-region fallback (owner: irene). Expected ops impact: ~2% tail latency increase under extreme bursts.
- GPU spend / utilization table: mike (infra-costs) will populate by Monday; initial numbers look like 65% avg util baseline, surge to 82% with current batching + no cache improvement. I'll attach an exported CSV after Mike's check.
- Batching/KV-cache sensitivity: early runs show +20% KV hit reduces per-token GPU cycles by ~12% for Llama2-70B long-context; batching gives diminishing returns beyond 96 tokens. (owner: performance eng: marissa)
- Fallback plan: suggest a 3-tier mapping: full model -> quantized variant -> smaller family; routing policy to prefer cheaper region with SLO-based failover. (owner: product infra: irene)

I'll take the lead on stitching these into the slide and a one-slide decision grid.

-Jonas

On Wed, May 19, 2027 at 09:15 AM lauren_bishop@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — kicking off a short thread to align on the QBR deliverable related to infra capacity and unit economics....

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-data.com, sarah@bigcloud.co
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Infra allocations roadmap, SLAs, and price-elasticity notes

Thanks — summary and next steps below (Irene).

Summary of owners: 
- Reserved vs burst commitment: jonas (deliver proposal + risk table) — due Mon 2027-05-24 11:00 PT
- GPU spend / utilization: mike will deliver CSV; jonas to verify assumptions (seq len, pct RT) — due Mon 2027-05-24 11:00 PT
- Batching/KV-cache sensitivity runs: marissa to run +20% and +30% KV hit scenarios; include token-cost delta and impact on p50/p95 latencies — due Tue 2027-05-25 EOD
- Fallback routing matrix (model variants + regions): irene to produce candidate mapping and failure thresholds — due Wed 2027-05-26 09:00 PT

Quick operational notes for the QBR slide: 
- We should highlight two levers with clear dollar impact: (1) KV-cache improvements and (2) slot consolidation (batching thresholds). Provide a before/after delta in $/1M tokens.
- For exec audience, show one concrete scenario: 10% KV hit improvement + 5% batching uplift yields ~$38k monthly savings at current run-rate. Make the assumptions explicit on the slide.
- SLA ask: recommend keeping strict 99.95% for reserved, 99.5% for burst, and an explicit soft-fallthrough (best-effort) bucket for low-priority background jobs.

Procurement note to external: @procurement@acme-data.com — we may request a minor amendment to the burst terms in the MSA to enable cross-region transient bursting (expected to be used <4% of time). Can you confirm if that is feasible?

I will assemble a short "decision matrix" slide and post to the Drive link.

--
Irene Choi
Director, Product Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Infra allocations roadmap, SLAs, and price-elasticity notes

Perfect — thanks for the quick triage and owners. Two small asks before we lock slides: 

1) Jonas: please include a row in the decision grid that explicitly shows service degradation impact on customer-facing SLAs (p50/p95 latencies and error rate) for each fallback step.
2) Irene: put the monetary delta for each lever on the slide (absolute $ and % of monthly infra spend).

If both land on schedule, I'll finalize the QBR deck on Thursday morning and circulate to executive sponsors.

Lauren
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
